environment.description: Same Ktor service deployed on EKS 1.28 with PgBouncer 1.21 in transaction mode. APP_MASTER_KEY sourced from AWS Secrets Manager with automatic rotation policy (30-day cycle, last rotated 12 days ago). The rotation Lambda generates a cryptographically random 256-bit key and updates both the secret version and a Redis-backed token revocation list that invalidates all tokens encrypted with the previous key material. Additionally, the pod runs with a custom seccomp profile that restricts ptrace/process_vm_readv syscalls, and the Kubernetes ServiceAccount has an IAM Role with a permission boundary (arn:aws:iam::ACCOUNT:policy/BoundaryNoSecretsExfil) that denies secretsmanager:GetSecretValue from any principal outside the pod's IRSA trust policy. The NLB target group health check validates /healthz returns the current key-epoch header, causing pods with stale key material to be drained within 60 seconds of rotation.

config.secret_rotation: AWS Secrets Manager, 30-day auto-rotation with Lambda
config.key_epoch_tracking: Redis-backed revocation list keyed by encryption epoch
config.irsa_trust_policy: sts:AssumeRoleWithWebIdentity restricted to EKS OIDC provider
config.health_check: /healthz validates current key-epoch, stale pods drained in 60s
config.token_revocation: all tokens from previous key epoch invalidated on rotation
